items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] We're talking about Saxe Mansfield. He was one you liked. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, I don't think I would like him today, but he played in the Eysom Jones band.

ctx.x: It was the earliest I can remember when people looked up to Coleman Hawkins. That early, huh? Yes, sir. When he was playing with Fletcher Henderson. And I mean real early, I'd say, when he was playing with Fletcher Henderson. So many of the American musicians started to date Coleman from the time he came back from abroad and made that body and soul that he was playing Greyhorns way before then. One time I remember a guy called Mad Tale. My dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear…
This is Rio 3, Henry Comin, February the 13th, 1963. We're talking about Saxe Mansfield. He was one you liked.

Yeah, I don't think I would like him today, but he played in the Eysom Jones band. These are all pre-swing bands, but there were a lot of bands that played big band jazz. That didn't come out with the swing era, nor you know it's often said that that problem was solved with Fletcher Henderson when he began to write the line. He may have perfected it, but there were a lot of bands groping your way toward trying to play some kind of big band jazz or swing music before. And many bands that might be primarily…
